ui.actions.facts_line: {author}: account {age} days old, {merged} merged here before, workflow files touched: {files}
ui.actions.choose_environment: This run waits for several environments. Choose one:
ui.actions.why_keep_alive: Quiet repository, days left before GitHub switches the schedule off:
ui.actions.vulnerable: Repositories with critical or high dependency alerts
ui.actions.unread: Not read (not the same as clean)
ui.actions.alert_again: {repo}: {workflow} failed again after its single automatic re-run

cli.actions.summary: waiting for a person {person}, failing lanes {red}, behind {behind}, vulnerable {vulnerable}, not read {unread}, proposals {proposals}
cfg.h.teamwork.enabled: Reads pull requests, alerts and waiting runs to show the views. Writing on GitHub also needs the actions on GitHub to be on, each action allowed and confirmed. Off by default.
cfg.h.teamwork.repos_per_cycle: How many repositories are read each time.
cfg.f.teamwork.refresh_hours: Hours between reads of a repository
cfg.h.teamwork.refresh_hours: The least time before a repository is read again.
cfg.f.teamwork.dismiss_days: Days a red run stays set aside
cfg.h.teamwork.dismiss_days: A set aside run comes back after this time, or as soon as there is a newer run.
cfg.h.teamwork.hide_workflows: Names or patterns, one per line.
cfg.h.teamwork.bot_authors: A pull request by one of them is a dependency update.
cfg.h.teamwork.bot_branches: A branch that matches is a dependency update.
cfg.h.teamwork.bot_labels: A pull request with one of these labels is a dependency update.
cfg.h.teamwork.dismissed_alerts: Lists who dismissed an alert, why and when.
cfg.h.teamwork.dismiss_allowed: A dismissal by anybody else raises an alert; empty: no comparison.
cfg.f.teamwork.auto_rerun: Re-run once by itself after an infrastructure failure
cfg.h.teamwork.auto_rerun: The only action that needs no confirmation: a run that did not start or timed out is re-run once, with the actions on GitHub on and rerun_failed allowed. A second failure raises an alert.
cfg.h.teamwork.cancel_policy: Patterns. Matching runs are only proposed for cancellation.
cfg.f.teamwork.queued_hours: Hours queued before proposing to cancel
cfg.h.teamwork.queued_hours: A run queued longer than this is proposed for cancellation.
cfg.f.teamwork.stuck_hours: Hours running before proposing a forced cancel
cfg.h.teamwork.stuck_hours: A run that has been going for longer is proposed for a forced cancel.
cfg.f.teamwork.forks_help: Facts about authors of fork runs
cfg.h.teamwork.forks_help: Before approving: age of the account, merged changes here and workflow files touched. A few extra reads each time you ask.
cfg.f.teamwork.inactive_workflows: Find workflows switched off for inactivity
cfg.f.teamwork.keep_alive_days: Quiet days before proposing to keep a schedule alive
cfg.h.teamwork.keep_alive_days: In a public repository with no push for this many days, proposes enabling its scheduled workflows again before GitHub switches them off at 60 days (GitHub does not document that this restarts its count; a new commit does). 0 = off.
cfg.f.teamwork.runner_hooks: Accept events of self-hosted runner hooks
cfg.h.teamwork.runner_hooks: The command runner-hook, run by the hook on this computer, records job start and end.
